newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore, Egypt to boost ties with investment deal.
newsitem.headline: Singapore, Egypt to boost ties with investment deal.

text.p: Singapore and Egypt said on Tuesday they would sign an investment agreement to strengthen bilateral ties.
The agreement, which was to be signed on Tuesday, aims to give investors more confidence and protection in the business projects of both countries, a government statement said.

Tuesday was the first day of a three-day visit by Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri to Singapore to boost trade and other ties. He arrived in the afternoon from Malaysia, where he announced agreement on four joint Egyptian-Malaysian projects.
The Singapore-Egypt investment guarantee deal provides for most favoured nation treatment with regard to investments.

It also agrees to freely convert and transfer compensation in the event of expropriation and nationalisation, and to refer investment disputes not settled within six months to the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes.
"This agreement demonstrates the strong bilateral relations both countries enjoy with each other," the statement said.
"It will also give investors from both Egypt and Singapore greater confidence and protection when investing in each other's country."

Ganzouri was met in Singapore by Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong. Ganzouri, making the first official visit to Singapore by an Egyptian prime minister, will also meet with President Ong Teng Cheong and Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew.
Total trade between Egypt and Singapore for 1996, including crude oil and petroleum products, amounted to Singapore $332.7 million (US$224.1 million), government figures show.
Singapore imported S$156.3 million from Egypt, and exported S$176.4 million in return.
Ganzouri leaves Singapore for Beijing on Thursday.
